summary: This note is a short biography of E. D. Gleason (Ernest Dewey Gleason, 1899–1959), a Democrat who served in the Louisiana House of Representatives from the Evergreen Community north of Minden in Webster Parish. He served from 1952 until his death at the end of his second term, and his widow, Mary Smith Gleason, was then appointed by Governor Earl Kemp Long to fill the remaining eight months of his term.
one_line: E. D. Gleason was a Democratic Louisiana state representative from Webster Parish who served from 1952 until his death in 1959.
key_facts: E. D. Gleason was also known as Ernest Dewey Gleason.
E. D. Gleason was born on September 9, 1899.
E. D. Gleason died on July 25, 1959.
E. D. Gleason was a Democratic member of the Louisiana House of Representatives.
E. D. Gleason represented the Evergreen Community north of Minden in Webster Parish in northwestern Louisiana.
E. D. Gleason served in the Louisiana House from 1952 until his death at the end of his second term.
Mary Smith Gleason, the widow of E. D. Gleason, was briefly his successor in office.
Mary Smith Gleason was appointed to serve the remaining eight months of the term by Governor Earl Kemp Long.
The note describes Earl Kemp Long as the governor who appointed Mary Smith Gleason.
